messages:
sophie: Heads-up — customer hit a hard schema validation error when using tool/function call for a payments workflow. They sent request id abc123def and a curl repro. Error is a 422 with an enum mismatch on `status`. Posting what I have so we can collect the full debug bundle.
ben: Thanks — can you paste the exact curl and the error payload? Also which model + runtime? :eyes:
sophie: Curl (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tool/call \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: abc123def' \
  -d '{"tool":"payment-processor","input":{"amount":1200,"currency":"USD","user_id":"u-987"}}'
```
sophie: Error body from customer (copied):
```
HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity
{
  "error": "schema_validation",
  "message": "Invalid enum value for field 'status'",
  "details": "received 'ok' but allowed values are ['success','failed']",
  "request_id": "abc123def"
}
```
raj: Hm. That payload suggests the function returned `status: "ok"` which is not allowed by the tool's JSON schema. Two possibilities: (1) model generation returned the wrong enum, or (2) our post-processing/normalization step mapped values incorrectly. Do we have the full function output or the runtime logs for that request?
sophie: Customer attached a tiny log snippet and a screenshot. Log shows our runtime forwarded a function output JSON:
```
{"tool":"payment-processor","result":{"status":"ok","tx_id":"tx_42"}}
```
sophie: They say sometimes it works, sometimes it returns 200 with `status: "success"`. So it's intermittent.
ben: Intermittent = either model nondeterminism or a routing/mapping bug. We should collect: full server-side runtime logs for abc123def (info/debug level), the model variant (model_name + model_version), sequence of fallback/routing decisions, any quantization/profile in use, and client-side timing. I'll open a debug-bundle request to infra.
infra-bot: Debug bundle request created: bundle-id dbg-1912345678-1. Upload URL: https://internal-s3/redwood/debug/dbg-1912345678-1.zip (presigned - expires in 72h). Please upload customer logs and the curl thread.
lina: Quick note — audit shows a minor deploy of normalization code 10 hours ago. Deploy tag: normalization-v1.3.2. Rolling back to v1.3.1 removed a microfix that added a lower-case map. Could be related.
raj: Good find. If normalization-v1.3.2 applied a permissive mapping like mapping "ok" -> "success" but then later revert changed behavior, that could cause intermittency depending on which instance handled the request. But the error shows we did not map, so maybe some instances have the mapping and some do not.
ben: Action plan:
- Sophie: get full runtime log bundle (dbg id above) + customer curl + client logs (request timing, retries)
- Raj: check rollout state for normalization-v1.3.2 across regions and pods, and grep for the mapping code
- Lina: check if any canary/partial rollout flags were toggled in the last 12h
- Infra-bot: collect traces/span for abc123def (trace id when available)
sophie: Uploaded what customer provided to the debug bundle URL. Added repro curl and screenshot. Also included the customer's reported latency: p95 ~1200ms on those failing requests.
raj: I'll grep logs for abc123def across the runtime cluster. If we see different instances returning different payloads, that points to a rollout inconsistency. If all instances are consistent, then model-level nondeterminism more likely.
ben: Also capture the exact schema used for the tool: can someone paste the tool schema here? We need to confirm allowed enum values.
lina: Tool schema snippet (from registry):
```
{
  "name":"payment-processor",
  "output":{
    "type":"object",
    "properties":{
      "status":{"type":"string","enum":["success","failed"]},
      "tx_id":{"type":"string"}
    },
    "required":["status","tx_id"]
  }
}
```
raj: Confirmed. No `ok` allowed. Next step: runtime logs + model output samples. Sophie, can you ask customer to run the curl with an extra header to force sticky routing to a single region/pod to see if that reduces flakiness? Suggest `-H 'X-Prefer-Region: us-west-2'` and include `-H 'X-Request-ID: abc123def-step2'`.
sophie: Will ask. Also asked for the client's SDK version — they are on 0.9.1. There's a known bug in 0.9.1 that retried requests without preserving deterministic seeds; could cause double requests to different backends.
ben: Good catch. If SDK retries with new seeds it could create nondeterministic model outputs and then the first success gets cached but the failed one surfaces. Need to know whether the failing responses come from a first attempt or a retry. Trace should show that.
infra-bot: Traces attached to bundle dbg-1912345678-1: span ids 0x1a2b... (partial). Link in bundle.
raj: I'll run a quick grep on the runtime for the normalization-v1.3.2 flag and instance hashes. If mismatch found, we can hotfix to make mapping deterministic server-side (e.g., normalize any "ok" -> "success" before schema validation) while we track down root cause.
ben: Also verify if any billing/auth 401s happened around that request time — user mentioned earlier a weird 401 for a different flow. Not likely related but good to rule out (auth errors sometimes trigger fallback codepaths).
sophie: Customer responded they will try the sticky-region curl and send back results, and they've exported more logs to the bundle. I'll update when they reply.
raj: I'll follow up with a short patch we can ship if we confirm inconsistent instances: add a schema-normalizer that maps common synonyms to allowed enums and re-run validation. That reduces customer impact while we fix rollout.
ben: Sounds good. Keep me updated. :thumbsup:
sophie: Upload complete. Marking this as escalated-high. I'll post final bundle link here once infra confirms upload integrity.
infra-bot: Bundle dbg-1912345678-1 verified (sha256: abcdef...)
sophie: Thanks everyone — I'll paste the final reproduction steps and the customer's sticky-region result when available.
